data.cultural_impact: The name Suhaylah, originating from the Arabic language, brings to mind the rich cultural heritage of the Islamic faith and its connection to the night journey of Prophet Muhammad (Peace Be Upon Him) described in the Qur'an in Chapter 17, known as Al-Isra' Wal-Miraj (Night Journey and Ascension). This name holds a deep connection to the Islamic tradition and serves as a reminder of the spiritual significance of nocturnal travel and the prophetic journey towards spiritual enlightenment.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic teachings, the name Suhaylah holds a profound spiritual significance, evoking the essence of the night journey that Prophet Muhammad (Peace Be Upon Him) embarked upon during his life. The journey during the night of Al-Isra' and Al-Miraj (624 CE) symbolizes escaping from the material world and being spiritually transported to the Sacred House of God (The Kabah), representing the innermost journey towards self-purification, devotion, and the ultimate goal of nearness to Allah. This mounts a deep spiritual belief that the name Suhaylah reflects the journey towards a more enlightened and God-centered existence.
